segments.text: CHAPTER 4 Blockchain-Based Secure and Energy-Efficient Privacy-Preserving Authentication Protocol for Internet of Vehicles Using Optimized El-Gamal Encryption 4.1 Preamble
segments.label: human

segments.text: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Vehicles has intensified the need for more advanced security mechanisms that can operate efficiently in highly dynamic and large-scale vehicular environments. Although blockchain-based authentication frameworks provide decentralization and data integrity, relying on a single security layer is often insufficient to counter sophisticated cyber threats and privacy breaches. The increasing volume of vehicular data, strict latency requirements, and frequent vehicle mobility demand authentication schemes that not only ensure strong security but also maintain low computational overhead and real-time responsiveness. To address these emerging challenges, this chapter proposes an enhanced authentication framework that integrates deep learning techniques with optimized cryptographic mechanisms within a blockchain-enabled IoV environment. By combining intelligent learning models with secure encryption strategies, the proposed approach aims to strengthen attack detection accuracy, preserve user privacy, and improve system efficiency. This chapter builds upon the foundation established in the previous chapter and introduces a more robust and scalable solution designed to meet the security and performance requirements of next-generation IoV networks.

segments.text: 4.2 Introduction
segments.label: human

segments.text: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has emerged as a key component of intelligent transportation systems by enabling seamless communication among vehicles, roadside infrastructure, and traffic management entities through On-Board Units (OBUs) and Roadside Units (RSUs). This interconnected environment significantly improves driving safety, traffic efficiency, and overall road utilization by supporting real-time
segments.label: ai_generated

segments.text: information exchange and cooperative decision-making (Aman et al., 2021; Qureshi et al., 2022). However, the rapid growth of IoV networks and their open communication nature have also introduced serious security and privacy challenges. Authentication is the first and most critical line of defense in IoV systems. Without proper authentication, malicious vehicles can easily join the network and perform harmful actions, such as impersonating emergency vehicles to bypass traffic regulations or injecting false traffic information to mislead other drivers (Chai et al., 2022). In addition, message integrity is equally important, as tampered data may still appear trustworthy to receiving vehicles, potentially leading to unsafe driving decisions and severe consequences (Xu et al., 2021). Therefore, ensuring message authenticity, integrity, non-repudiation, and traceability is essential for secure IoV communications. Privacy preservation is another major concern in IoV environments, since vehicles continuously generate sensitive data such as location, identity, and movement patterns. Although traceability is required to identify and penalize misbehaving vehicles, unrestricted disclosure of vehicle information can result in unauthorized tracking and privacy violations (Kaltakis et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2021). Conditional privacy-preserving mechanisms aim to balance these conflicting requirements by protecting vehicle anonymity under normal conditions while enabling identity revelation when malicious behavior is detected. Traditional IoV security solutions largely rely on centralized authorities, which suffer from single-point-of-failure issues, limited scalability, delayed response times, and vulnerability to insider attacks (Zhang and Wu, 2021; Kebande et al., 2021). Moreover, centralized trust models struggle to handle the dynamic topology and high mobility of vehicular networks, making them inadequate for next-generation IoV applications. To overcome these limitations, decentralized and intelligent security mechanisms are required.
segments.label: ai_generated

segments.text: Blockchain technology has gained significant attention as a promising solution for IoV security due to its decentralized architecture, immutability, and cryptographic trust mechanisms. By distributing consensus among participating nodes, blockchain enables secure data sharing without relying on a trusted third party (Shen et al., 2022; Tu et al., 2023). However, blockchain-based IoV systems often incur high computational, storage, and communication overhead, particularly during consensus operations and key management processes (Xie et al., 2023). Furthermore, the massive volume of vehicular data can lead to network congestion and latency. To address these challenges, intelligent learning techniques and optimized cryptographic mechanisms are increasingly integrated into blockchain-enabled IoV systems. Deep learning models can effectively detect malicious activities by analyzing complex traffic patterns, while optimized encryption schemes can ensure data confidentiality with reduced computational cost (Wang et al., 2022; Ghimire and Rawat, 2022). Motivated by these advancements, this work proposes a systematic blockchain-based privacy-preserving authentication protocol that combines deep learning-based attack detection with optimized El-Gamal encryption for secure and efficient IoV communications.

segments.text: 4.2.1 Why Blockchain in IoV
segments.label: human

segments.text: IoV networks operate in highly dynamic and decentralized environments where vehicles frequently join and leave the network. In such scenarios, centralized security architectures become vulnerable to single-point failures, data manipulation, and trust management issues. Blockchain addresses these challenges by providing a decentralized and tamper-resistant ledger that records all transactions in an immutable manner (Chattaraj et al., 2021; Shen et al., 2022). Through consensus mechanisms, blockchain ensures that only valid and authenticated information is accepted by the network. Additionally, blockchain leverages cryptographic techniques to protect sensitive vehicular data, such as vehicle identities and locations, from unauthorized access.
segments.label: ai_generated

segments.text: Secure peer-to-peer communication enabled by blockchain eliminates the need for intermediaries, thereby reducing latency and improving reliability for time-sensitive IoV applications (Wu et al., 2023). These features make blockchain a suitable foundation for building secure, trustworthy, and privacy-aware IoV authentication systems.

segments.text: 4.2.2 IoV Use Cases
segments.label: human

segments.text: The proposed blockchain-based privacy-preserving authentication protocol supports several critical IoV applications. In real-time traffic management, authenticated and trustworthy data sharing among vehicles enables efficient route optimization and congestion control. For vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-infrastructure payments, blockchain facilitates secure and decentralized financial transactions, such as toll collection and parking fee payments, without relying on centralized payment gateways. In accident reporting systems, blockchain ensures immutable storage of event data, which is crucial for insurance claims and legal investigations. Furthermore, autonomous driving applications rely heavily on trusted communication among vehicles to coordinate maneuvers and ensure safety. In all these use cases, strong authentication and privacy preservation are essential, and the proposed protocol is designed to meet these requirements effectively. 4.3 Systematic View of IoV Network and Dataset Characteristics with

segments.text: Blockchain-Based Storage 4.3.1 System View of the Internet of Vehicles Network
segments.label: human

segments.text: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) represents a large-scale intelligent networking paradigm that integrates smart transportation technologies with Internet of Things (IoT) concepts to extend the capabilities of traditional Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs). By enabling continuous interaction among vehicles, infrastructure, users, and cloud platforms, IoV supports a wide range of applications such as intelligent
segments.label: ai_generated

segments.text: traffic management, collision avoidance, emergency response, autonomous driving, infotainment services, and smart navigation (Aman et al., 2021; Qureshi et al., 2022). An IoV ecosystem is composed of several interconnected entities that collaboratively enable intelligent transportation services. Vehicles are equipped with On-Board Units (OBUs), sensors, and communication modules that collect and transmit real-time vehicular and environmental data. Drivers and passengers interact with these systems to access safety and convenience services. Roadside Units (RSUs), deployed along roadways, act as intermediate communication points that facilitate data exchange between vehicles and backend infrastructure. In addition, cloud servers provide large-scale data storage, analytics, and decision support, while a Central Authority (CA) is traditionally responsible for network registration, credential management, and access control (Xu et al., 2021; Kebande et al., 2021). Through the periodic exchange of safety-related messages, such as beacon or safety broadcast messages, vehicles form a dynamic and socially connected network of smart objects. This interaction allows vehicles to share traffic conditions, road hazards, and driving intentions in real time. Due to the coexistence of heterogeneous users, devices, and services, IoV is classified as a heterogeneous network. Its highly dynamic topology, strict latency requirements, and continuous data generation introduce significant challenges in terms of scalability, reliability, and security (Kaltakis et al., 2021). Conventionally, the IoV architecture follows a layered design that relies on centralized trust management through a central authority. This architecture can be broadly described using four functional layers. The environment sensing and control layer is responsible for collecting raw data through vehicle-mounted sensors. These sensors capture information related to vehicle status, surrounding traffic, road conditions, positioning systems, and wireless signal characteristics. The network access and transport layer manages communication protocols, node connectivity, data validation, and message dissemination between vehicles, RSUs, and infrastructure.
segments.label: ai_generated

segments.text: The coordination and computing layer handles data processing, resource scheduling, and system management functions. This layer often interacts with cloud or edge computing platforms to support real-time analytics and decision-making. Finally, the application layer provides end-user services by analyzing processed data and responding to safety-critical or convenience-oriented events. Applications at this layer include traffic safety alerts, route optimization, infotainment services, and emergency management. These services can be further categorized into open services, such as real-time traffic updates accessible to all vehicles, and cloud-based services, including centralized traffic monitoring and control platforms (Shen et al., 2022; Tu et al., 2023). A conceptual illustration of the IoV system architecture is presented in Fig. 4.1, highlighting the interaction among vehicles, RSUs, cloud services, and management entities.

segments.text: 4.3.2 Dataset Details
segments.label: human

segments.text: To validate the proposed authentication and privacy-preserving framework, vehicular data are obtained from the Highway Safety Research Dataset maintained by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). This dataset contains comprehensive information related to road traffic scenarios, including vehicle crash records, traffic flow characteristics, and sensor-generated vehicular data collected from real IoV environments across major highways in the United States. Unlike commonly used generic datasets, this source provides realistic and trustworthy data suitable for evaluating security, authentication, and collision-related behaviors in IoV systems. The dataset includes key attributes such as vehicle speed, positional information, traffic conditions, and accident occurrences. For this study, approximately 50,000 data records are utilized to ensure reliable performance assessment and meaningful experimental analysis.

segments.text: 4.3.3 Data Storage in Blockchain​
segments.label: human

segments.text: The vehicular data collected from the data source are securely stored using 𝐼𝑣 blockchain technology. Blockchain functions as a distributed and shared digital ledger that records transactions among entities that do not necessarily trust one another. Once stored, the data become tamper-resistant, as the ledger is append-only and updated sequentially through a series of interconnected blocks. Each block typically contains the cryptographic hash of the previous block, a timestamp, and the transaction records. This chained structure ensures data integrity, since any attempt to modify stored information would alter the block hash and invalidate all subsequent blocks unless the entire chain is recomputed. Blockchain networks are commonly classified into public blockchains, where any participant can join and validate transactions, and private blockchains, which restrict access to authorized entities only. In IoV environments, this flexibility allows blockchain deployment to be tailored according to security and access control requirements.
segments.label: ai_generated

segments.text: The adoption of blockchain for vehicular data management offers several key advantages. Immutability ensures that once a block is added, its content cannot be altered without detection. The distributed ledger mechanism enables all participating nodes to maintain synchronized copies of the ledger, enhancing transparency and trust. The consensus mechanism defines the rules by which blocks are validated and appended, ensuring agreement among network participants. In addition, smart contracts—self-executing code deployed on the blockchain—automate transaction validation and authentication once predefined conditions are met. By leveraging these features, blockchain effectively addresses security vulnerabilities, trust issues, and centralized failures in vehicular networks. In the proposed system, smart contracts are utilized to securely record vehicular data and support authentication operations within the IoV framework. 4.3.4 Authentication Mechanism Using Cascaded and Dilated Residual RNN in the IoV Platform Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are employed in this work to support the authentication process within the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) environment. RNNs are well known for their effectiveness in handling sequential data, as they maintain internal memory that captures temporal relationships between consecutive inputs. This capability makes RNNs particularly suitable for IoV authentication tasks, where vehicle messages and network behaviors follow time-dependent patterns. By learning historical dependencies, the model can distinguish between legitimate and malicious transmission behaviors more accurately. As highlighted by Elman (1990) and later extended by Hochreiter and Schmidhuber (1997), RNN-based models are capable of modeling long-term dependencies that are essential for security-sensitive applications. In the proposed framework, the authentication decision is generated iteratively across time steps, where the network updates its hidden state and output based on both the current input and the previously learned context, enabling reliable and continuous authentication in dynamic IoV networks.

The RRNN architecture decomposes the learning process into two interconnected stages. In the first stage, a linear model captures the primary trend of the sequential data. In the second stage, the residual error produced by this linear approximation is forwarded to the RNN, which focuses exclusively on learning the remaining nonlinear patterns. By integrating linear estimation with nonlinear sequence modeling, the RRNN efficiently exploits both characteristics of IoV data. This residual learning mechanism offers two major advantages. First, combining linear and nonlinear representations improves prediction and authentication performance compared to using either approach independently. Second, since the RNN is trained only on residual errors rather than the entire signal, the training process becomes faster, more stable, and computationally less complex. As a result, RRNNs are particularly well suited for IoV authentication tasks where accuracy, scalability, and training efficiency are critical.

Proposed CD-RRNN for Authentication- The proposed Cascaded Dilated Residual Recurrent Neural Network (CD-RRNN) is employed to strengthen the authentication mechanism in the IoV environment. Although the Residual Recurrent Neural Network (RRNN) provides faster training and improved learning efficiency, it still faces limitations in fully identifying sophisticated malicious behaviors and is susceptible to gradient degradation when processing long sequential data. To overcome these drawbacks, dilation is integrated into the residual recurrent structure. The dilated RRNN, inspired by the dilated recurrent architecture introduced by Chang et al., 2017, adopts a multi-layer and cell-independent design with hierarchical skip connections across different time steps. These dilated skip connections enable the network to capture long-range temporal dependencies while significantly reducing the risk of vanishing gradients. In addition, dilation allows the model to operate with fewer parameters, improving computational efficiency without sacrificing detection capability. By stacking multiple dilated recurrent layers with varying dilation rates, the CD-RRNN achieves multi-resolution temporal learning, making it highly effective for time-sensitive authentication tasks in IoV networks. segments.text: 4.3.5 Addressing IoV Security and Privacy Challenges
segments.label: human

segments.text: The proposed authentication protocol is designed to effectively address the key challenges inherent in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) environments, such as high mobility, rapidly changing network topologies, and stringent privacy requirements. The decentralized nature of blockchain eliminates dependence on static centralized servers, thereby avoiding single points of failure and improving resilience under dynamic vehicular conditions. Timestamped and hash-linked blocks ensure the integrity and consistency of vehicular data across distributed nodes, even during frequent topology changes. To handle sequential and time-dependent vehicular data, the proposed CD-RRNN processes traffic patterns using dilated skip connections, enabling robust detection of malicious behavior despite continuous node movement. This architecture enhances adaptability to real-time network variations while maintaining detection accuracy. Furthermore, privacy and traceability are jointly preserved through conditional privacy mechanisms. Transactions are stored in an anonymized manner on the blockchain, while smart contracts allow authorized entities to trace malicious vehicles only when suspicious behavior is detected. The Optimized Key El-Gamal Encryption (OKEE), supported by MMRFO-based key generation, dynamically adapts encryption strength to network conditions, reducing latency and improving scalability without compromising confidentiality.

segments.text: ​ Figure 4.3: Flowchart of designed MMRFO for producing the optimal key ElGamal Encryption Scheme- ElGamal encryption, originally introduced by Taher ElGamal (1985), is a well-known asymmetric cryptographic technique derived from the Diffie–Hellman key exchange principle. It relies on the computational hardness of the discrete logarithm problem and supports both secure encryption and digital signature generation. Unlike deterministic public-key cryptosystems, ElGamal
segments.label: human

segments.text: Deployed OKEE for Data Privacy Preservation- To ensure strong privacy protection for vehicular data, this work introduces an Optimized Key ElGamal Encryption (OKEE) mechanism. In conventional ElGamal encryption, cryptographic keys are generated using random parameters, which ensures security but may lead to increased computational overhead and inefficient memory usage. To overcome these limitations, the proposed OKEE framework integrates an intelligent optimization strategy to generate cryptographic keys that are both secure and resource-efficient. ElGamal encryption, originally proposed by ElGamal (1985), is widely adopted in secure communication systems due to its resistance to discrete logarithm attacks. However, its performance and security are highly dependent on the quality of the generated keys. In this research, the Modified Manta Ray Foraging Optimization (MMRFO) algorithm is employed to optimally generate encryption keys. By leveraging fitness-driven search behavior, MMRFO selects keys that minimize system complexity while enhancing resistance against emerging cryptographic attacks. The optimized key generation process aims to reduce memory consumption and computational time, making the encryption process suitable for real-time IoV environments. The generated optimal key also strengthens protection against sophisticated adversaries by increasing the unpredictability of cryptographic parameters. Additionally, optimized key selection simplifies key management and improves scalability across large vehicular networks. segments.text: Exemplary Illustration of the Proposed Scheme- The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) significantly improves transportation efficiency and road safety by enabling seamless communication among vehicles, infrastructure, and surrounding entities. Through Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) interactions, IoV supports advanced intelligent transportation applications, where authentication plays a critical role in verifying the legitimacy and reliability of exchanged vehicular data. Authentication serves as the
segments.label: ai_generated

segments.text: first line of defense against malicious activities, ensuring that only authorized vehicles and infrastructure nodes participate in network communications. Despite its importance, existing authentication solutions predominantly depend on centralized architectures, which introduce serious security and privacy vulnerabilities. Such approaches often suffer from issues including vehicle trajectory leakage, excessive reliance on roadside units (RSUs) and cloud servers, high computational complexity, and single-point-of-failure risks. These limitations significantly weaken the resilience of IoV systems in highly dynamic and large-scale vehicular environments. Blockchain technology offers a promising alternative by providing a decentralized and tamper-resistant framework for authentication. By integrating smart contracts, cryptographic primitives, and consensus mechanisms, blockchain establishes a trusted environment without requiring centralized control. However, the decentralized nature of blockchain also introduces challenges related to increased storage requirements, communication overhead, and computational cost. Moreover, the inherent transparency of blockchain-based IoV systems can expose sensitive vehicular information if privacy mechanisms are not carefully designed. To overcome these challenges, this work proposes an efficient blockchain-enabled authentication scheme that balances security, privacy, and system performance. The proposed approach minimizes the shortcomings of traditional authentication mechanisms while preserving data confidentiality and trust among participating entities. The overall workflow of the proposed scheme is illustrated in Fig. 4.5, demonstrating how secure authentication and privacy preservation are achieved within the IoV environment.

segments.text: In this work, a secure and efficient blockchain-enabled authentication and privacy preservation framework is developed for Internet of Vehicles (IoV) environments. Initially, relevant vehicular data are extracted from a benchmark dataset and provided to the proposed Cascaded and Dilated Residual Recurrent Neural Network (CD-RRNN) to identify malicious activities. By integrating residual learning with dilation and cascading mechanisms, the CD-RRNN effectively captures temporal dependencies and improves threat detection accuracy. The verified and authenticated data are then stored across distributed blockchain blocks to ensure integrity and tamper resistance. Subsequently, privacy protection is achieved through an Optimized Key El-Gamal Encryption (OKEE) scheme, where cryptographic keys are optimally generated using the Modified Manta Ray Foraging Optimization (MMRFO) algorithm. This optimization strategy significantly reduces computational overhead and memory consumption while strengthening security. Finally, the performance of the proposed framework is extensively evaluated and compared with existing conventional methods to demonstrate its superior effectiveness in secure IoV communications.

segments.text: The proposed blockchain-based authentication and privacy-preserving framework for Internet of Vehicles (IoV) was implemented using the Python programming environment to evaluate its effectiveness under realistic conditions. The experimental configuration for the Modified Manta Ray Foraging Optimization (MMRFO) algorithm consisted of a population size of 10, a chromosome length of 16, and a maximum of 50 iterations to ensure stable convergence and reliable optimization outcomes. To assess malicious attack detection performance, several well-known learning models were employed for comparison, including the Deep Neural Network proposed by Kang and Kang (2016), Support Vector Machine introduced by Hoang et al. (2021), Long Short-Term Memory network presented by Ashraf et al. (2020), and the classical Recurrent Neural Network described by Yufeng Wang et al. (2019). For optimization validation, traditional metaheuristic algorithms such as the Tunicate Swarm Algorithm developed by Kaur et al. (2020), the Golden Eagle Optimizer proposed by Mohammadi-Balani et al. (2021), Harris Hawks Optimization introduced by Heidari et al. (2019), and the original Manta Ray Foraging Optimization by Weiguo Zhao et al. (2020) were considered. In addition, the cryptographic performance of the proposed Optimized Key El-Gamal Encryption (OKEE) was evaluated against standard encryption techniques, including Data Encryption Standard described by Guo et al. (2020), Advanced Encryption Standard reviewed by Hidayat and Mahardiko (2024), Elliptic Curve Cryptography discussed by El-Zawawy et al. (2022), and the classical El-Gamal encryption implemented by Imran et al. (2020). The experimental implementation was carried out using Python 3.9 on a system equipped with an Intel Core i7-9700K processor operating at 3.6 GHz, 32 GB RAM, and an NVIDIA RTX 2080 Ti GPU. segments.label: ai_generated
